result.report_text:
# Initial rates: dataset.csv

## Verdict

- [treated] Michaelis-Menten: the data give no evidence of substrate inhibition (p = 1) or cooperativity (Hill, p = 0.0684).
- [treated] Substrate inhibition with Ksi above 6.19 ppm is not excluded; rates at [S] approaching that would show it or rule it out.
- [treated] Michaelis-Menten: Vmax 212.7 (197.3 to 229.3 counts/min/min), Km 0.06412 (0.04692 to 0.08616 ppm) (95% profile intervals).
- [untreated] The data reject Michaelis-Menten in favour of the Hill law (p = 0.0232).
- [untreated] The Hill exponent is below 1 (n = 0.621): the rate rises more gradually with [S] than Michaelis-Menten allows. Negative cooperativity, a mixture of enzyme forms with different Km, or an error that changes with [S] all do this, and the exponent cannot say which.
- [untreated] Two alternatives were tested, each at 0.05, so the chance that at least one rejects a true Michaelis-Menten law is up to 0.0975.
- [untreated] Hill: Vmax 195.1 (160.1 to 399 counts/min/min), K0.5 0.08241 (0.04204 to 2.583 ppm), n 0.6207 (0.3334 to 0.9288) (95% profile intervals).
- Between groups: Vmax differs between treated and untreated: sharing it fits worse than separate values (F(1, 19) = 25.5, p = 7.08e-05).
- Between groups: Km: no difference between treated and untreated detectable by these data (F(1, 19) = 1.72, p = 0.206); the shared fit gives Km = 0.05797 (0.04599 to 0.07234). Not detected is not the same as equal.
- Literature: Km [treated], michaelis-menten: the substrate column is in 'ppm', which cannot be converted to a molar concentration without a molar mass the file does not give; a literature comparison needs a molar unit.
- Literature: Km [untreated], hill: the Hill law has no Km (its K0.5 is the concentration at half Vmax of a sigmoid, not a Michaelis constant), so it is not compared with a cited Km.

## The data

23 rate(s) at 12 distinct condition(s) (11 replicate row(s)), in 2 groups by 'state': treated (12), untreated (11).
Units: substrate in ppm (not convertible to molar: fitted as given, and not comparable with a cited constant); rate in counts/min/min (an arbitrary unit: fitted as given).
Uncertainty: estimated from the fit's own residuals (ordinary least squares), which assumes the model is right.
The groups' own verdicts differ or are undecided (treated: michaelis-menten; untreated: hill), so the comparison of constants between groups uses the michaelis-menten law for all.
Read --organism 'human' as Homo sapiens.

## Michaelis-Menten (treated)

`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S])`

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 212.7 | 6.947 | 197.3 to 229.3 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.06412 | 0.008281 | 0.04692 to 0.08616 | ppm |

- Residual standard error 10.93 counts/min/min on 10 degrees of freedom. No goodness-of-fit chi-square is given: sigma was estimated from these residuals, so the chi-square is 10 by construction and cannot test the law it was computed from.
- Correlations of the estimates: Vmax-Km +0.765.
- Starts: 6 of 6 reached this minimum; no start found a different one.
- Condition number of the weighted Jacobian (log constants): 6.38.
- Lack of fit: lack of fit F = 1.07 on 4 and 6 degrees of freedom, p = 0.447: no departure from this law's shape beyond the replicates' own scatter.
- Substrate range: Your 6 substrate concentration(s) span 0.31 to 17 times Km (below Km: 2; above: 4; in the guideline range of 0.2 to 5 times Km: 4). The Assay Guidance Manual asks for 8 or more in that range, with several on each side of Km.
- Substrate range: The range brackets Km with fewer than 8 concentrations in the guideline range. Eight concentrations evenly spaced on a log scale from 0.2 times the lowest to 5 times the highest Km in its interval would satisfy the guideline wherever Km lies: 0.0094, 0.016, 0.028, 0.048, 0.084, 0.14, 0.25, 0.43 ppm.

## The laws tested (treated)

| restricted law | general law | restriction | kind | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| michaelis-menten | substrate-inhibition | Ksi -> infinity | boundary (50:50 mixture) | F(1, 9) = 0 | 1 | not ruled out |
| michaelis-menten | hill | n = 1 | interior | F(1, 9) = 4.285 | 0.0684 | not ruled out |

Ruled out means p below 0.05, a convention; every p-value is printed so another can be applied. A boundary restriction (a constant going to infinity) is tested against the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self & Liang 1987): half the ordinary p-value.


Substrate inhibition (Haldane), for comparison (`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S] + [S]^2 / Ksi)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 212.7 | 7.323 | 196.3 to 247.8 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.06412 | 0.008729 | 0.04587 to 0.09591 | ppm |
| Ksi | not determined | - | > 6.192 (no upper bound) | ppm |

Ksi ran to the edge of the search; the standard errors above are conditional on it being held there, so they can understate the uncertainty the profile intervals beside them show.

- Ksi > 6.192 ppm: the data do not determine an upper bound. No substrate inhibition is detectable in this range; it would show at [S] approaching 6.19 ppm or above.

Hill, for comparison (`v = Vmax [S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 237.9 | 20.4 | 206.4 to 329.9 | counts/min/min |
| K0.5 | 0.08588 | 0.02434 | 0.05436 to 0.3074 | ppm |
| n | 0.7394 | 0.1226 | 0.4759 to 1.026 | - |

## Hill (untreated)

`v = Vmax [S]^n / (K0.5^n + [S]^n)`

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 195.1 | 25.37 | 160.1 to 399 | counts/min/min |
| K0.5 | 0.08241 | 0.03928 | 0.04204 to 2.583 | ppm |
| n | 0.6207 | 0.1304 | 0.3334 to 0.9288 | - |

- Residual standard error 7.366 counts/min/min on 8 degrees of freedom. No goodness-of-fit chi-square is given: sigma was estimated from these residuals, so the chi-square is 8 by construction and cannot test the law it was computed from.
- Correlations of the estimates: Vmax-K0.5 +0.983, Vmax-n -0.930, K0.5-n -0.897.
- Starts: 7 of 7 reached this minimum; no start found a different one.
- Condition number of the weighted Jacobian (log constants): 28.5.
- Lack of fit: lack of fit F = 0.155 on 3 and 5 degrees of freedom, p = 0.922: no departure from this law's shape beyond the replicates' own scatter.
- Substrate range: Your 6 substrate concentration(s) span 0.24 to 13 times K0.5 (below K0.5: 2; above: 4; in the guideline range of 0.2 to 5 times K0.5: 4). The Assay Guidance Manual asks for 8 or more in that range, with several on each side of K0.5.
- Substrate range: The range brackets K0.5 with fewer than 8 concentrations in the guideline range. Eight concentrations evenly spaced on a log scale from 0.2 times the lowest to 5 times the highest K0.5 in its interval would satisfy the guideline wherever K0.5 lies: 0.0084, 0.024, 0.068, 0.2, 0.56, 1.6, 4.5, 13 ppm.

## The laws tested (untreated)

| restricted law | general law | restriction | kind | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| michaelis-menten | substrate-inhibition | Ksi -> infinity | boundary (50:50 mixture) | F(1, 8) = 0 | 1 | not ruled out |
| michaelis-menten | hill | n = 1 | interior | F(1, 8) = 7.844 | 0.0232 | ruled out |

Ruled out means p below 0.05, a convention; every p-value is printed so another can be applied. A boundary restriction (a constant going to infinity) is tested against the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self & Liang 1987): half the ordinary p-value.


Michaelis-Menten, for comparison (`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S])`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 160.3 | 6.48 | 145.6 to 176.5 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.04771 | 0.007782 | 0.03137 to 0.07006 | ppm |

Substrate inhibition (Haldane), for comparison (`v = Vmax [S] / (Km + [S] + [S]^2 / Ksi)`):

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | 160.3 | 6.873 | 144.5 to 187.6 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.04771 | 0.008254 | 0.03025 to 0.07615 | ppm |
| Ksi | not determined | - | > 5.334 (no upper bound) | ppm |

Ksi ran to the edge of the search; the standard errors above are conditional on it being held there, so they can understate the uncertainty the profile intervals beside them show.

- Ksi > 5.334 ppm: the data do not determine an upper bound. No substrate inhibition is detectable in this range; it would show at [S] approaching 5.33 ppm or above.

## Between groups (Michaelis-Menten)

| shared constant | statistic | p | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax | F(1, 19) = 25.52 | 7.08e-05 | differs |
| Km | F(1, 19) = 1.718 | 0.206 | no difference detected |
| all | F(2, 19) = 24.14 | 6.07e-06 | the groups differ |

- Vmax differs between treated and untreated: sharing it fits worse than separate values (F(1, 19) = 25.5, p = 7.08e-05).
- Km: no difference between treated and untreated detectable by these data (F(1, 19) = 1.72, p = 0.206); the shared fit gives Km = 0.05797 (0.04599 to 0.07234). Not detected is not the same as equal.
- The F tests pool the scatter of every group's separate fit, which assumes each group was measured with the same precision; each group's own residual standard error is in its section above.

The fit with Km shared:

| constant | estimate | standard error | 95% profile interval | unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vmax [treated] | 208.6 | 5.804 | 196.4 to 221.5 | counts/min/min |
| Vmax [untreated] | 166.6 | 5.807 | 154.6 to 179.3 | counts/min/min |
| Km | 0.05797 | 0.00591 | 0.04599 to 0.07234 | ppm |

## Against the literature

- Km [treated], michaelis-menten: the substrate column is in 'ppm', which cannot be converted to a molar concentration without a molar mass the file does not give; a literature comparison needs a molar unit.
- Km [untreated], hill: the Hill law has no Km (its K0.5 is the concentration at half Vmax of a sigmoid, not a Michaelis constant), so it is not compared with a cited Km.

Cited values from BRENDA (Chang et al. 2021, Nucleic Acids Res. 49:D498, doi:10.1093/nar/gkaa1025), through Caterva's literature resolver.

## What these numbers are

- FITTED to this file's rates, under the law named, not measured constants: their provenance is this dataset and this law, and they are conditional on both.
- Intervals are 95% profile-likelihood intervals (Bates & Watts 1988); the standard errors are asymptotic and are what a +-2 SE interval would be built from, which for Km is often too symmetric.
- A fit this good is not evidence that the law is right; the tests above compare the laws fitted, and a law not fitted was not considered.
- References: Cornish-Bowden A. Fundamentals of Enzyme Kinetics, 4th ed. Wiley-Blackwell, 2012 (rate laws). Segel IH. Enzyme Kinetics. Wiley, 1975 (inhibition laws). Bates DM, Watts DG. Nonlinear Regression Analysis and Its Applications. Wiley, 1988 (profile intervals). Self SG, Liang KY. J. Am. Stat. Assoc. 82:605 (1987) (tests on the boundary). Draper NR, Smith H. Applied Regression Analysis. Wiley (lack of fit and pure error). Hurvich CM, Tsai CL. Biometrika 76:297 (1989) (AICc). Brooks HB et al. Basics of Enzymatic Assays for HTS. Assay Guidance Manual, NCBI Bookshelf NBK92007 (the 0.2-5 Km design range).
result.methods: Initial rates (23 measurements at 12 distinct conditions, in 2 groups; substrate in ppm, rate in counts/min/min) were fitted to the Michaelis-Menten, substrate inhibition (Haldane), Hill rate laws (Cornish-Bowden 2012; Segel 1975) by nonlinear least squares (scipy.optimize.least_squares, trust-region reflective, on the logarithms of the constants, which keeps them positive; derivatives by the complex step; multiple starting points spread across the range of the data). Rates were weighted equally (ordinary least squares) and the standard deviation was estimated from the residuals, which assumes the rate law is correct. 95% confidence intervals are profile-likelihood intervals (Bates & Watts 1988), bounded by the profile-t statistic against Student's t on the residual degrees of freedom; asymptotic standard errors are also reported. Nested rate laws were compared by likelihood-ratio tests (chi-square with the error known, extra-sum-of-squares F with it estimated); restrictions that put a constant at infinity were referred to the 50:50 mixture of chi-square(0) and chi-square(1) (Self & Liang 1987), and non-nested laws were described by AICc (Hurvich & Tsai 1989) without a test. Lack of fit was tested against pure error from replicates (Draper & Smith). Differences between groups were tested by fitting each constant shared across groups and comparing with separate fits. The table (23 measurements used) was read by Caterva Studio from the file puromycin.csv (one measurement per row). Software: Caterva 0.5.0 (caterva rates), Python 3.12.13, NumPy 2.2.6, SciPy 1.15.3.
